title: rwb-integration EFS hand-over: the mount of the step, the split across four owners, the consumed contract paths, the run summary store and the level of the decision record are not settled by any one source
source: WP B-P2-01; legacy RWB-E2-001; Ownership Map v1 (interaction, efs_ledger_outcome and reconciliation_result to P1; recovery_case and case_account to P3; decision_log_entry to P7; GET /admin/jobs, POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun, GET /data-products/freshness and POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions to P1); FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 (inbound source loads and EFS out of scope) and AC-EXC-P2-007-07; TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1 (P2 reads the views) and T5.2 (P2 calls nothing in P1 for inbound data); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 15, 16, 41, 43, 44 and 45; RWB-ITG-E2001-ITG section 3 and section 11
description: One combined gap covers everything this slice cannot read from a single source. (1) The legacy story is one Quartz job inside one service; under D-RCV-60 the same journey is four owners, and the split is fixed only by the plan, the Ownership Map and RWB-ITG-E2001-ITG: case creation, the account link and CaseCreated to rwb-case; the EFS history read and the interaction append to rwb-source-data; the central ledger to rwb-decision; the hand-over step, the group builder and the run summary stay with rwb-integration. (2) Two sources place the work elsewhere: FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 puts every inbound source load, EFS included, out of P2 scope because ACE ingests it, and TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2 still has P2 reading the ACE views directly and calling nothing in P1; both are superseded by DP-05 and ADR-010, and the conflict is recorded, not hidden. (3) The rwb-integration login name (DP-02) is given nowhere; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc login. (4) The paths, query parameters and JSON field names of the consumed rwb-source-data operations for the eligible accounts, the customer row and the reconciliation result are not in any source, and neither is the rwb-case case-creation path (the Ownership Map publishes GET /cases and POST /cases/{caseId}/actions but no create operation), although the legacy interface CaseCreation.createOrLink names the operation. (5) JOB-02 stays rwb-case's per the Ownership Map and Arch v5 slide 44, while the legacy story started JOB-02 for the hand-over; the step therefore runs on AceDataReady in rwb-integration and the rerun operation POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun is P1's, so the refusal of a second start is split between P1's door and this step's run lock. (6) The legacy run summary was written to reconciliation_result and to the batch step; in the target reconciliation_result is P1's and job_catalog holds a catalogue row, not a run, so no table of rwb-integration holds a run summary. (7) The legacy story left the creation decision to the decision log writer; with DP-03 each owner writes its own record, and no source says whether the hand-over step writes a record of its own run or only the case owner writes one. (8) MSG-P1-001 is worded differently in the legacy story and in FSD P2 Integration v3 VR-P2-001-1.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-001 section 4 step 1 (JOB-02 starts when AceDataReady arrives) and step 9 (run summary to reconciliation_result); section 12 (Job JOB-02, HandoverRun, and the four in-process interfaces CaseCreation, InteractionLedger, AccountQuery, EfsHistoryQuery); section 13 (HandoverJob, no new table, processed_event and reconciliation_result written). TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1 ('P2 reads source data only through recovery.v_ace_* views') and T5.2 ('P2 reads the views in T1.1 directly and calls nothing in P1 for inbound data'). FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 ('Out of scope: Every inbound source load: ALS, SCBPDM, EFS ...') and VR-P2-001-1 (MSG-P1-001 '{product} is from {date}. Today's data is not yet complete.'). Architecture v5 slide 44 (JOB-02 owner rwb-case, mechanism AceDataReady -> DailyCaseRun) and slide 45 ('Only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views (ADR-010)'). Ownership Map v1 rows for interaction, efs_ledger_outcome, reconciliation_result, recovery_case, case_account, decision_log_entry, job_catalog and the four P1 operations.
area: Integration ownership, consumed contracts and run record
proposed: Keep the split recorded by RWB-ITG-E2001-ITG and the Ownership Map and mark TSD P2 v3 T5.2 and the P2 inbound exclusion as superseded by DP-05 and ADR-010 in the Service Contract Catalog; agree the consumed operation paths and field names at the contract review of RWB-P2-E2001-CON with the P1 and P3 owners; hold the run summary in the activity result, one local decision record and the REC-01 row written through P1, with no table of rwb-integration; name the login before the rwb_integration baseline is created.

title: rwb-integration EFS hand-over contract: the activity contract, the consumed element shapes, the provided surface and the fakes have no source text
source: WP B-P2-01; legacy RWB-E2-001 section 12; RWB-P2-E2001-APP; RWB-P2-E2001-CON; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (P2 IN: GET /interface-runs, POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry; OUT: FileDelivered, FileFailed); TSD P2 Integration v3 T-A.1; Ownership Map v1
description: The contract this slice needs does not exist in the source set. (1) The legacy story fixes a Java interface HandoverRun with one method returning a summary of read, created, linked, repeats, held and gap dates, and four in-process interfaces; nothing fixes a workflow name, activity names, inputs, outputs, a retry policy or a summary element list, so every one of them is a default of this story. (2) Architecture v5 slide 16 and TSD P2 v3 T-A.1 give rwb-integration only the interface-run operations and the outbound-file events; no source gives a hand-over operation, and the step is event-started, so the slice provides no REST operation at all. (3) The element names of the six consumed rwb-source-data operations, the rwb-case case-creation answer (created or linked, linked from, is primary) and the decision-record failure class are not in any source. (4) The error mapping from a failing owner answer to MSG-P1-001, MSG-P2-007, MSG-P7-003, MSG-P2-006, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-GEN-006 is implied by the legacy exception table and by the FSD exception flows, and is fixed here as a default. (5) MSG-P1-001 has two wordings; the FSD P2 Integration v3 wording is used and the legacy wording is not repaired.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-001 section 12 ('Published interface built (package recovery.integration.handover.api): public interface HandoverRun { HandoverSummary run(LocalDate businessDate); }') and the exception table MSG-P1-001, MSG-P2-007, MSG-P7-003, MSG-P2-006, MSG-P4-002. FSD P2 Integration v3 AC-EXC-P2-007-03, AC-EXC-P2-007-06, AC-EXC-P2-007-07 and VR-P2-001-1. Architecture v5 slide 16 (P2 contract, no hand-over path) and slide 44 (JOB-02 with rwb-case). TSD P2 Integration v3 T-A.1 API-P2-001 to API-P2-014 (no hand-over operation).
proposed: Fix the workflow, the nine activities, the twelve summary elements and the retry policy in contract/handover-run-activities.yaml; fix the six P1 elements and the P3 element in the two consumed contracts with the element names of this story as the default; carry the placeholder for every path and field name the source does not give; publish the six fakes from the owners' OpenAPI documents and fail the build on drift.

title: rwb-integration EFS hand-over deployment: the values, the alert identifiers, the dashboard series and the runbook have no source
source: WP B-P2-01; legacy RWB-E2-001 sections 4, 5 and 14; RWB-P2-E2001-OPS; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 32, 33 and 41; Architecture Decision Records v3 ADR-023; Non Functional Specification v3
description: The deployment of the step is a new artefact with no source text. (1) The legacy story names one feature flag and one hold time; nothing gives replica counts, resource sizes, probe paths and timings, lag thresholds, alert thresholds, consumer group name, retry intervals or the build ID format, so all of them are environment values and placeholders. (2) The legacy story raises a late-batch alert and an incident, and the FSD names MSG-P1-001, MSG-P2-001, MSG-P2-006 and MSG-P7-003; no source names a message id for a lagging hand-over group or for a consumed AceDataReady that started no run, so both carry the placeholder. (3) No source names the dashboard series of the hand-over or its dimensions; ADR-023 fixes observability per service and the six series here — accounts read, cases created, accounts linked, repeats, held, gap dates — are the default. (4) No source names the runbook entries, their owner roles or the runbook location. (5) The smoke-run fixture owner and the synthetic business date are not given.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-001 sections 4, 5 (X2, X6, X7) and 14 (MSG-P1-001, MSG-P2-007, MSG-P7-003, MSG-P2-006, MSG-P4-002); section 13 (feature flag rwb.integration.efs-handover). Architecture v5 slide 33 (rwb-comms and rwb-integration share the 16:00 window) and slide 41 (one login, one topic, one queue, one schema per service). Architecture Decision Records v3 ADR-023 (observability per service). Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-052, NFR-053 and NFR-054 (secrets, encryption, pipeline checks).
proposed: Fix the chart, the one consumer group, the registration step, the migration step, the six series, the four alerts and the four runbook entries in this story; keep every environment value in a values file and every missing message id as a placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names it; review the runbook with the on-call rota before the release date.
